Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss GCB's Q3 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, our Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. GCB delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover four key areas: competitive activity and our responses, capital expenditure plans, promotional strategy and effectiveness, and supply chain efficiencies along with their productivity impacts. I'll now turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $7.5 billion, representing a 5.2% increase compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 48.2%, driven by supply chain productivity savings, favorable product mix, and disciplined pricing actions. Operating income was $1.36 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.12. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me now turn to the competitive landscape and our strategic responses, which have been a key focus amid a dynamic CPG environment characterized by moderating inflation, persistent private label pressure, and accelerating innovation cycles. As you know, the industry saw Nielsen-measured CPG dollar sales growth of just 2.1% in Q3 across tracked channels, down from 4.5% a year ago, driven by softer volume trends at -1.2% and deflationary pricing in select categories like snacks and household cleaners. Our team has been proactive in monitoring and countering competitive moves, leveraging IRI and Circana data for real-time ACV tracking and velocity insights.

Starting with North America, which represents 55% of our revenue and where competition remains fiercest. Procter & Gamble and Kimberly-Clark intensified promotional activity in the paper products and baby care segments, with P&G's Huggies line posting a 150 bps market share gain to 28.5% in diapers via aggressive Everyday Low Pricing and targeted shopper marketing. Their trade spend as a percentage of revenue ticked up to 22% from 19% year-over-year, funding 15% deeper discounts and expanded end-cap displays, capturing 2.3 points of ACV in mass channels. Unilever, meanwhile, launched a reformulated Dove Men+Care portfolio with 20% more moisturizers, backed by a $75 million advertising and promotion blitz across digital and linear TV, driving 8% volume uplift and pressuring our men's grooming SKUs.

Our response has been multifaceted and disciplined. We countered P&G's diaper push by reallocating $45 million in trade funding to our flagship GCB TenderCare line, achieving 12% deeper funding on average—equivalent to a 25% increase in off-invoice allowances. This stabilized our diaper market share at 22.1%, flat year-over-year, while improving household penetration by 1.8 points to 87% ACV. In grooming, we accelerated our "Clean Slate" innovation pipeline, rolling out bio-based, recyclable packaging for our GCB Edge shave gels, which resonated with sustainability-focused Gen Z shoppers. Paired with a 30% uplift in e-commerce velocity via Amazon Sponsored Brands and Shopify partnerships, we clawed back 80 bps in share, ending the quarter at 14.2%. Importantly, these actions kept our trade spend efficiency at 18% of revenue, below the category average of 20.5%, preserving gross margins at 48.2%.

Shifting to EMEA, where macroeconomic headwinds like Germany's 8.5% VAT hike on non-essentials amplified price sensitivity, private labels from Aldi and Lidl gained 320 bps combined in household care, reaching 42% share. Reckitt Benckiser's Lysol disinfectant sprays, reformulated for 99.9% virus kill claims with essential oils, stole 1.5 points from us through €50 million in pan-regional sampling and in-store demos, boosting their velocity by 11% in discounters. Nestlé's entry into plant-based snacks with Garden Gourmet—claiming 30% less sodium—further eroded our savory portfolio.

We responded with precision targeting. In the UK and France, we launched a "Value Defense" program, mirroring EDLP with 10-12% list price resets on core laundry SKUs, supported by 25% more trade promotions in high-traffic Tesco and Carrefour aisles. This stemmed private label bleed, limiting our share loss to just 40 bps in laundry to 26.8%. For snacks, our R&D team fast-tracked a €30 million investment in high-protein, air-fried chips under GCB CrunchMax, hitting 15g protein per serving—outrunning Nestlé's specs. Distributed via a dedicated Doritos-style partnership with PepsiCo's Frito-Lay network for co-branded displays, we achieved 22% trial rates per Kantar data and grew APAC-like velocity in EMEA hypermarkets. Regionally, this drove 3.2% volume recovery, with e-commerce sales up 28% year-over-year via Ocado and Amazon Pantry exclusives.

In APAC, growth hotspots like India and China faced dual threats: local players like Patanjali in India ramping Ayurvedic personal care with 18% cheaper positioning, gaining 250 bps to 12% share, and premium incumbents like L'Oréal pushing K-beauty dupes in China. Overall, category volumes contracted 0.8% amid urban slowdowns, per Euromonitor.

Our playbook here emphasized localization and digital. In India, we matched Patanjali's pricing with a 15% reset on GCB HerbalGlow shampoos, bundled with Reliance Retail loyalty apps for 2-for-1 redemptions, stabilizing share at 19.4%. In China, we countered L'Oréal via Tmall Live streams, investing RMB 100 million in influencer seeding for our GCB SilkEssence serums with hyaluronic acid boosts. This yielded 35% e-com growth, capturing 4.1 points of Tmall ACV and flipping share positive by 60 bps to 16.7%. A key technical initiative was our AI-driven "Promo Optimizer" tool, rolled out across APAC, which uses machine learning on 10 million+ transaction records to predict competitive pricing 72 hours ahead, boosting response ROI by 27%.

Latin America rounded out the picture, with inflation at 9.2% in Brazil fueling 5%+ private label expansion at Walmart Mexico and GPA banners. Colgate-Palmolive's Total toothpaste variants with 12-hour protection claims drove 9% sales uplift via 20% more sampling.

We leaned into our "Fortaleza Forte" platform—Portuguese for "strong fortress"—deploying 18% higher trade dollars in Brazil for GCB MaxShield dentifrice, achieving 14% velocity gains and limiting share erosion to 30 bps. In Mexico, cross-category bundling with Bimbo baked goods secured 2.5 extra shelf facings per store, per IRI.

Strategically, these responses underscore our "Defend, Differentiate, Disrupt" framework. We've defended core volumes through optimized trade spend—up 12% year-over-year but with 15% better return on marketing—differentiated via 28 new SKUs from our $250 million annual R&D budget, emphasizing clean-label and upcycled ingredients amid 65% consumer demand for sustainability per our proprietary shopper panels. And we've disrupted with tech: our blockchain-traced supply chain for cocoa products countered Barry Callebaut's pricing wars, ensuring 98% on-shelf availability versus peers' 92%.

Looking forward, we expect competitive intensity to persist into FY25, with peers like Mondelez signaling 5-7% A&P hikes. We'll counter with $1.2 billion in targeted investments, including expanded precision marketing via The Trade Desk and our first-mover CPG metaverse activations on Roblox for Gen Alpha trials. Early tests show 40% higher engagement than TikTok. Net-net, these actions position us to gain 50-75 bps in aggregate market share, targeting 12.5% category-leading position by year-end.

Next, I'd like to discuss our capital expenditure plans and priorities, which remain a cornerstone of our strategy to drive sustainable growth in this dynamic CPG landscape. As you know, we've been navigating a mix of inflationary pressures on raw materials—like the 15-20% uplift in palm oil and PET resin costs we've seen industry-wide—while capitalizing on strong consumer tailwinds in health & wellness and premium snacks. Our disciplined approach to capex ensures we're not just maintaining our 25%+ EBITDA margins but positioning for mid-single-digit top-line growth through FY26.

For FY24, we're guiding to total capital expenditures of $1.25 billion, representing about 4.2% of our projected net sales of $29.8 billion. That's a modest 8% increase year-over-year from the $1.16 billion we deployed in FY23, reflecting our focus on high-ROI projects with average payback periods under 3.5 years. We've already committed 72% of this budget through Q3, on track and under budget by 2%, thanks to favorable supplier negotiations and our in-house engineering teams optimizing project timelines.

Let me break this down by our four key priority pillars, which align tightly with our 'Resilient Growth 2027' strategy—emphasizing supply chain agility, sustainability, digital transformation, and capacity for high-growth SKUs.

First, manufacturing and supply chain resilience, which accounts for 42% or $525 million of our FY24 capex. Post the 2022 supply disruptions that hit peers like Unilever and Mondelez with 5-10% cost headwinds, we've prioritized brownfield expansions and greenfield sites in stable, low-cost regions. In North America, we're investing $180 million to upgrade our flagship facility in Toledo, Ohio—home to our VitaSnacks protein bars and plant-based lines—with state-of-the-art high-speed fillers and robotic palletizers from Krones and Fanuc. This will boost output by 25%, targeting the 12% CAGR in better-for-you snacks, where we're gaining share against Kellogg and General Mills.

Regionally, Europe gets $120 million for our expanded aseptic processing plant in Rotterdam, Netherlands, focused on our FreshEssence ambient beverages. This addresses the EU's stringent sustainability regs under the Green Deal, incorporating 40% recycled content in packaging ahead of 2025 mandates. In emerging markets, $150 million is earmarked for a new greenfield plant in Guadalajara, Mexico, leveraging nearshoring trends to serve LATAM and mitigate U.S.-China tariff risks—similar to how Colgate has fortified its oral care supply in the region. Expect 10-15% efficiency gains here, reducing our total cost per case by 8% through FY25.

Second, sustainability initiatives, 25% or $310 million. ESG isn't a buzzword for us—it's ROI-positive. We're on track to hit our 2030 net-zero Scope 1 & 2 goals five years early, with $140 million going to solar microgrids and heat pump retrofits across 15 North American and APAC sites. For instance, our PureHome cleaning products plant in Singapore will install a 5MW solar array, cutting energy costs by 30% and generating 10,000 MWh annually—mirroring P&G's successful model at their West Virginia facility. Water stewardship is another focus: $90 million for advanced recycling systems in water-stressed India and Brazil, recycling 80% of process water for our personal care lines. This not only de-risks us from droughts impacting 20% of global ag supply but also appeals to 65% of Gen Z consumers prioritizing eco-brands, per Nielsen data.

Third, digital and automation transformation, 22% or $275 million. We're accelerating our Industry 4.0 playbook to counter labor shortages—up 18% in CPG warehousing per BLS stats—and improve forecast accuracy amid volatile demand. $110 million funds AI-driven demand sensing platforms from Blue Yonder, integrated with IoT sensors on 500+ production lines, aiming to reduce stockouts by 40% and working capital by 5-7 days. In distribution, we're rolling out $85 million in automated micro-fulfillment centers with AutoStore systems in key U.S. hubs like Dallas and Chicago, supporting our e-comm growth to 22% of sales, up from 15% in FY22. This positions us competitively against Amazon's encroachment in grocery, much like PepsiCo's investments in their direct-to-consumer tech stack.

Finally, R&D and innovation facilities, 11% or $140 million. To fuel our 15%+ pipeline of new product launches—like the zero-sugar FreshEssence RTD coffees launching Q1 FY25—we're expanding our Global Innovation Center in Cincinnati by 50,000 sq ft. This includes high-throughput prototyping labs for precision fermentation in plant-based dairy alternatives, targeting the $20B global market growing at 14% CAGR.

Looking ahead, FY25 capex guidance is $1.3-1.4 billion, or 4.3-4.5% of sales, with a continued 40/30/20/10 split across these pillars. We're financing this 85% from operating cash flow—projected at $3.2 billion—keeping leverage steady at 2.1x net debt/EBITDA. These investments underpin our 6-8% organic sales growth outlook, with ROIC expansion to 18% by FY26.

We're excited about the leverage these capex dollars will provide as consumer spending normalizes and premiumization trends persist.

Turning now to our promotional strategy and its effectiveness, which continues to be a cornerstone of our revenue growth engine in this dynamic CPG landscape. With inflation cooling but still pressuring household budgets—U.S. grocery inflation hovered at 1.2% year-over-year per Nielsen data—our promotions have been laser-focused on driving volume, protecting market share, and optimizing returns amid heightened retailer scrutiny on trade terms.

In Q3, our total promotional spend reached $1.2 billion, up 8% year-over-year and representing 14.5% of net sales—slightly above our long-term target of 13-15% but a deliberate acceleration to counter softer category growth. This includes both trade promotions, 72% of spend, and consumer-facing activities, 28%. The effectiveness? Outstanding. Our blended return on promotion spend improved to 3.8x, up from 3.4x last year, driven by smarter targeting and execution. This translates to an incremental $4.6 billion in net revenue lift for the quarter, with volume up 2.1% ex-promos—our strongest in two years.

Breaking it down by core levers, our trade promotion strategy emphasized "right-sized" events tailored to retailer priorities. In North America, which accounted for 55% of our promo budget, we leaned into high-low pricing at key accounts like Walmart and Kroger. For instance, our flagship snack brand, CrispWave chips—our $2.5B powerhouse akin to PepsiCo's Lay's—saw a 15% off-shelf price promotion during back-to-school, delivering a 12% ACV lift and 4.2x ROPS. We avoided over-promoting staples like our household cleaner, PureShield, where we shifted to everyday low pricing at club stores like Costco, reducing promo intensity by 20% year-over-year while growing household penetration 3 points to 28%.

Consumer promotions, meanwhile, pivoted heavily digital—up 25% year-over-year to $340 million. Our app-based loyalty program, GCB Rewards, now boasts 45 million active users, an 18% increase, with personalized offers via machine learning algorithms predicting purchase elasticities down to the SKU level. Take our beverage portfolio: For ZestQuench energy drinks, competing in the Red Bull-dominated space, we ran geo-fenced push notifications offering 2-for-1 deals to high-propensity lapsed buyers, yielding a 22% redemption rate and 5.1x ROPS—well above our 4x hurdle rate.

On the technical front, we're not just spending smarter; we're optimizing with cutting-edge tools. Our PromoOptix AI platform, built in partnership with NielsenIQ and powered by advanced causal analytics, now forecasts promo lift with 92% accuracy, up from 85% last year. This incorporates real-time inputs like competitor pricing from Circana data, weather impacts on impulse buys, and even macroeconomic signals like consumer confidence indices. In Europe, where 25% of our spend goes, we've integrated this with retailer EDI systems at Tesco and Carrefour, enabling dynamic "event sizing"—auto-adjusting depth and duration based on baseline sales velocity. Result? Promo waste down 15% to under 8% of spend.

Regionally, the story varies. North America remains our promo powerhouse, with effectiveness highest at mass merchandisers, ROPS 4.2x, but challenged by Amazon's aggressive e-comm pricing, where our share dipped 1.2 points to 14%. We countered with sponsored product ads and Subscribe & Save bundles for personal care items like GlowEssence shampoos, recapturing 80bps. In EMEA, facing 2-3% deflation in dairy and a 10% VAT hike in select markets, we focused on "value packs" for our yogurt line, mirroring Danone's strategy—bundle sizes up 20%, driving 7% volume growth and shielding margins at 22.5% gross. Latin America, 15% of spend, grappled with currency volatility; here, hyper-local BOGO events via Mercado Libre partnerships lifted our tortilla chip brand, SaborMex, by 18% in Mexico, though ROPS moderated to 3.2x due to informal trade leakage.

Asia-Pacific, our growth engine at 5% of sales, saw the biggest strategic shift: from broad discounting to experiential promotions. In China, via Tmall and JD.com, we launched AR-enabled virtual try-ons for skincare, bundled with 30% off PureGlow serums—conversion rates hit 28%, rivaling L'Oréal's digital playbook, with ROPS at 4.5x. India emphasized kirana store sampling for our affordable soap brand, CleanWave, distributing 50 million samples and gaining 4 points share in a $10B market.

Trends shaping our approach? First, the death of blunt force promotions. With CPG promo elasticities declining 10-15% over five years per Kantar and IRI studies, we're prioritizing "precision promotion"—targeting top 20% of households that drive 80% of volume. Second, e-comm's rise: 22% of our promo dollars now digital, up from 12% in 2022, with headless CMS integrations for omnichannel consistency. Third, sustainability tie-ins: 15% of promotions featured eco-packaging calls-to-action, boosting brand favorability 8 points among Gen Z.

Strategically, we're balancing short-term tactics with long-term equity. Promo intensity on power brands like CrispWave is capped at 16% of sales to preserve premium pricing—ACV distribution steady at 95%. We've clawed back 150bps of trade spend from underperformers via zero-based budgeting, reallocating to high-ROI channels. Looking forward, Q4 guidance assumes flat promo spend as % of sales, targeting 4x+ ROPS amid holiday peak. Risks? Retailer consolidation, like the Kroger-Albertsons merger scrutiny, could pressure terms, but our diversified footprint mitigates this.

In sum, our promotional engine is firing on all cylinders—driving 52% of Q3 volume growth while expanding operating margins 90bps to 18.2%. This disciplined approach positions GCB to outperform peers like Unilever and Colgate, who reported softer ROPS amid similar inflation.

Finally, before I hand it back to Sarah for forward-looking guidance, I'd like to dive deep into our supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings, one of the standout performers this quarter. In the CPG space, where gross margins are often in the mid-teens to low-20s amid relentless input cost inflation from commodities like palm oil, PET resin, and propylene glycol, supply chain is our margin engine. This quarter, these initiatives delivered a $285 million headwind offset—or put another way, a 7.2% reduction in COGS as a percentage of sales year-over-year—directly contributing 120 basis points of gross margin expansion to our 48.2% consolidated gross margin.

Let me break this down systematically, starting with the P&L impact, then the balance sheet benefits, key technical levers we've pulled, regional nuances, and our strategic outlook. These aren't one-offs; they're structural, embedded in our 'Supply Chain 2025' roadmap, which targets $1.2 billion in cumulative savings by fiscal 2025, putting us ahead of peers like Procter & Gamble, who guided to $800 million in productivity this year, or Unilever's €800 million supply chain savings program.

P&L Impact: Layered Savings Across the Value Chain. Our efficiencies cascaded through procurement, manufacturing, and logistics, totaling $285 million in savings, up 18% from Q3 last year. Procurement led with $110 million, 38% of total, driven by strategic sourcing. We locked in multi-year contracts for key inputs—think sodium laureth sulfate for our laundry liquids and cocoa for our snack bars—yielding 9% savings on spot buys versus the 15% commodity inflation we saw in ags and chemicals. Manufacturing productivity added $95 million, 33%, with 4.2% yield improvements across our 45 global plants, particularly in high-volume categories like fabric care and oral care, where we're mirroring Colgate-Palmolive's precision cleaning tech.

Logistics and distribution rounded it out at $80 million, 28%, as we boosted on-time-in-full rates to 96.2% from 92% a year ago—critical in CPG where retailer fines for stockouts on shelf-stable goods like our Healthy Bites protein bars can hit 5% of invoice value. Overall, these flowed 65% to the bottom line, juicing adjusted EBITDA by $185 million and expanding EBITDA margins by 210 basis points to 25.3%.

Balance Sheet Wins: Working Capital Optimization. Beyond P&L, productivity slashed inventory by 12% sequentially to 68 days of supply, down from 82 days industry average per Nielsen data. This freed up $450 million in cash, reducing days payable outstanding to 75 days while extending supplier terms strategically without alienating partners. Days sales outstanding held steady at 28 days, thanks to our e-invoicing push with majors like Walmart and Tesco. Net-net, inventory turns improved to 5.4x from 4.7x, a metric where we're now lapping Kimberly-Clark's 5.2x.

Technical Initiatives: Tech-Enabled Transformation. These results stem from our heavy tech investments—$250 million capex this year, 40% of total—focusing on four pillars: 1. AI/ML Demand Sensing: Our proprietary 'ForecastX' platform, powered by partnerships with Blue Yonder and integrated with SAP IBP, reduced forecast error by 28% for volatile SKUs like seasonal personal care, such as sunblock lines. This cut safety stock by 15% without service hits. 2. Automation and Robotics: Deployed 150 AGVs across our North American DCs, mirroring Amazon's playbook but tailored for palletized CPG goods. In our Memphis hub, this slashed pick rates labor by 35%, with ROI in 18 months. 3. Digital Twin and Predictive Maintenance: Using Siemens MindSphere in 20 plants, we preempted $25 million in downtime from legacy bottling lines for beverages and cleaners, boosting overall equipment effectiveness to 88% from 82%. 4. Blockchain Traceability: Rolled out IBM Food Trust for 60% of our supply base, cutting dispute resolution from 45 to 7 days and enabling premium pricing on 'farm-to-shelf' claims for organic baby foods—up 3% on those tiers.

Sustainability ties in here too: These moves trimmed Scope 3 emissions by 11%, aligning with our SBTi net-zero pledge and unlocking rebates from EU carbon schemes.

Regional Commentary: Tailored Execution. Performance varied by geography, reflecting local dynamics: North America, 55% of sales: Star performer with $140 million savings, 9.5% COGS relief. Nearshoring from Mexico—up 25% in maquiladora capacity for household essentials—dodged West Coast port strikes and ILWU labor hikes, saving $40 million in ocean freight amid Red Sea disruptions. EMEA, 25% of sales: $75 million savings despite energy headwinds. UK and German plants optimized via variable-speed drives, offsetting €2.50/kWh gas prices post-Ukraine. OTIF hit 97.5% with Aldi and Carrefour, but inflation lingers on glass for our premium shampoos. APAC/LatAm, 20% of sales: $70 million, fueled by volume leverage in Indonesia and Brazil. Here, supplier consolidation with palm oil majors like Wilmar yielded 12% input savings, though China lockdowns added 2% air freight costs for beauty actives—we mitigated with regional hubs.

Strategic Insights and Peer Context. In CPG, where private label pressures from Costco and Lidl erode pricing power, these efficiencies are our moat. Unlike Reckitt's supply chain resets post-COVID, ours emphasize resilience—dual-sourcing 85% of critical inputs and stress-testing for 20% demand swings. Margins now stand at 48.2%, versus P&G's 24% target but ahead of Mondelez's 20%. Looking ahead, we see $300-350 million in Q4 savings, with upside from FX tailwinds in emerging markets. Risks? Persistent inflation in ocean rates, up 20% YTD per Drewry Index, and talent shortages in automation roles, but our 15% supply chain wage premium keeps attrition low.

This positions GCB for mid-single-digit organic growth with double-digit EPS expansion in FY24. With that, Sarah?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, Michael, for that comprehensive overview. Looking to the remainder of the year, we're confident in our trajectory, with Q4 guidance for net sales growth of 4-6% and adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.20, factoring in continued productivity and our defensive positioning. We're well-set to deliver on our full-year targets.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your consumer spending habits?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, John. Inflation has been moderating, as we noted, but persistent private label pressures and softer volumes industry-wide have made consumers more price-sensitive. In North America and EMEA, we've seen this in categories like snacks and household care, where we've countered with targeted pricing resets and deeper trade funding on core SKUs like TenderCare and PureShield. Our precision promotions via PromoOptix have helped drive volume recovery, with 2.1% ex-promo growth, and our sustainability-focused innovations are resonating with premium-seeking Gen Z, limiting downside. Overall, we're defending share while positioning for normalization.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with JPMorgan.

Emily Johnson:
Thanks. Regarding your new product CrunchMax high-protein chips, what are the projections for its market impact?

Lisa Patel:
Thanks, Emily. CrunchMax, with 15g protein per serving in air-fried format, is off to a strong start post-launch in EMEA and expanding to North America Q4. Early Kantar data shows 22% trial rates, outpacing Nestlé's plant-based entrants, thanks to our Frito-Lay co-branded displays and digital velocity boosts. We project $150 million in first-year sales, capturing 1-2 points share in savory snacks, with 20% repeat rates driven by e-comm exclusives on Ocado and Amazon. This fits our Disrupt pillar, fueling 3-5% category growth contribution in FY25.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley.

David Lee:
Can you provide more details on the promotional spending for the quarter?

Michael Chen:
Sure, David. As I detailed earlier, Q3 promo spend hit $1.2 billion, 14.5% of sales, up 8% year-over-year but with ROPS at a strong 3.8x. Trade was 72%, focused on right-sized events like the 15% off on CrispWave at Walmart, delivering 4.2x returns, while consumer digital jumped 25% via GCB Rewards' 45 million users. Our PromoOptix AI hit 92% lift accuracy, cutting waste 15%. Q4 flat as % of sales, targeting 4x+ amid holidays. This drove 52% of volume and 90bps op margin expansion.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.

aspect_summary.Competitive activity and response: Amid dynamic CPG environment with moderating inflation, private label pressure, and peer innovations (e.g., P&G/Kimberly-Clark in NA diapers, Unilever in grooming, Reckitt/Nestlé in EMEA, Patanjali/L'Oréal in APAC, Colgate in LATAM), GCB responded with targeted trade funding reallocations (e.g., $45M to TenderCare diapers), pricing resets, innovations (e.g., CrunchMax chips, bio-based packaging), digital strategies, and AI Promo Optimizer, stabilizing/gaining share via 'Defend, Differentiate, Disrupt' framework while keeping trade spend efficient at 18% of revenue; expect persistent intensity into FY25 countered by $1.2B investments.
aspect_summary.Capital expenditure plans and priorities: FY24 capex $1.25B (4.2% of $29.8B sales, up 8% YoY) prioritized across manufacturing/supply chain resilience (42%, $525M: NA/EU/EM expansions), sustainability (25%, $310M: solar, water recycling), digital/automation (22%, $275M: AI demand sensing, robotics), R&D/innovation (11%, $140M); FY25 $1.3-1.4B (4.3-4.5% sales), financed 85% by operating cash flow, targeting high-ROI (<3.5yr payback) for growth and margins.
aspect_summary.Promotional strategy and effectiveness: Q3 spend $1.2B (14.5% sales, up 8% YoY; trade 72%, consumer digital 28% up 25%) delivered 3.8x ROPS (up from 3.4x), $4.6B revenue lift, 2.1% ex-promo volume growth via right-sized trade events (e.g., 15% off CrispWave), digital loyalty (GCB Rewards 45M users), and PromoOptix AI (92% accuracy, 15% waste cut); regional tailoring (e.g., value packs EMEA, AR try-ons APAC); Q4 flat % targeting 4x+ ROPS.
aspect_summary.Supply chain efficiencies and productivi: Q3 savings $285M (+18% YoY; procurement $110M/38%, manufacturing $95M/33%, logistics $80M/28%) offset 7.2% COGS, expanded gross margin 120bps to 48.2%, cut inventory 12% (68 days, freeing $450M cash); driven by AI forecasting, robotics/AGVs, digital twin maintenance, blockchain; regional strengths (e.g., NA nearshoring); Q4 $300-350M outlook under 'Supply Chain 2025' targeting $1.2B cumulative by FY25.
